headings: Drive Restaurant Traffic and Build Sales
"You First" Culture Elevates Employee and Customer Satisfaction
Experienced, Passionate Leadership Team and Deep Bench of Talent
paragraphs: First Watch Restaurant Group, Inc. is a Delaware holding company. Unless the context otherwise requires, "we," "us," "our," "First Watch," the "Company," "Management" and other similar references refer to First Watch Restaurant Group, Inc. and, unless otherwise stated, all of its subsidiaries.

Since opening our doors in 1983, we have been a pioneer in Daytime Dining, serving made-to-order breakfast, brunch and lunch using the freshest of ingredients. We have built our brand on our commitment to operational excellence, our culinary mission centered around a fresh, continuously evolving menu, and our "You First" culture. Our focus on one daytime shift enables us to optimize restaurant operations while generating an average unit volume of $2.3 million per restaurant in 2025 in only 7.5 hours per day. This daytime focus also provides us with a competitive advantage, allowing us to attract and retain employees who are passionate about hospitality and drawn to our "No Night Shifts Ever" approach, among other attractive benefits.
As of December 28, 2025, we had a total of 633 restaurants across 32 states, 560 of which were company-owned and 73 of which were franchise-owned.

Every morning, thousands of our employees arrive at the crack of dawn to slice and juice fresh fruits and vegetables, bake muffins, brew our fresh coffee and whip up our French Toast batter from scratch. Every menu item is made-to-order and prepared with care. We do not use microwave ovens, heat lamps or deep fryers in our kitchens. At First Watch, we are driven by a pursuit of freshness as is highlighted by our culinary and sourcing philosophy to "Follow the Sun." With this philosophy, our menu, which is inspired by the seasons, changes four to five times per year. Our rotating seasonal menu is commonly cited by our customers as a core element of the First Watch experience and has included favorites such as the Parmesan and Prosciutto Toast, Chimichurri Steak and Eggs Hash, and the Brooklyn Breakfast Sandwich.

These seasonal items are offered alongside our award-winning chef-driven menu that includes elevated executions of classic favorites for breakfast, brunch and lunch, such as our protein-packed Breakfast Quinoa Bowl, Chickichanga and Avocado Toast. Our menu also features fresh juices, that we juice each morning, including Morning Meditation and Kale Tonic.

For over four decades, we have cultivated an organizational culture built on our foundational concept of "You First," which puts serving others above all else. As a company, we put our employees first and empower them to do whatever it takes to put our customers first. As evidenced by our vision to "Create Amazing Opportunities for Our People," we also work hard to provide our employees with opportunities for advancement and meaningful relationships, and we prioritize personal and professional growth so that our people can thrive. We believe our approach and operating model have enabled us to retain and attract the best and brightest employees in the industry and are key factors in our ability to meet our growing demand across the country. As a result, we are proud of the many people-focused awards and accolades we have received over the past few decades. For four consecutive years, First Watch has been named a Top 100 Most Loved Workplace® by the Best Practice Institute, and in 2025, was named the #1 Most Loved Workplace for the second year in a row, as featured in The Wall Street Journal. Also, in 2025, First Watch was named one of Yelp's Most Loved Brands nationwide.

We also extend our You First culture by giving back to important organizations and causes that are meaningful to our people and our communities. In addition to various local philanthropic efforts in the communities we serve, First Watch focuses its giving through key efforts designed to create positive impact both externally and within our organization:

•Project Sunrise: Through this initiative, we source our coffee beans from women-owned farms in Colombia, and we pay an annual quality incentive bonus to farmers to further support their high-quality production. This program in turn empowers these women leaders to reinvest in their communities.

•Pediatric Cancer Research: We donate a portion of the proceeds from each sale of a First Watch kid's meal to the V Foundation in order to support and advance pediatric cancer research. As of December 28, 2025, we have donated approximately $2.0 million toward this important effort.

•The You First Fund: Established in 2020, the You First Fund provides grants to eligible team members experiencing personal hardship related to qualifying disasters. The fund is intended to support employees and their immediate families during their times of most significant need and is funded through a portion of the proceeds from each kid's meal sale, along with contributions from the Company, our employees and others. Since its inception, this fund has provided our employees with over $1.1 million in hardship grants.

We believe First Watch has the potential for more than 2,200 restaurants in the continental United States. In 2021, First Watch was recognized by FSR Magazine as the fastest-growing full-service restaurant company in the United States based on unit growth. In 2025, we continued to realize that potential by opening 64 new company-owned and franchise-owned restaurants, which we collectively refer to as "system-wide" restaurants, across 23 states. Our growth strategy contemplates increasing the annual number of new system-wide restaurant openings.

In selecting new locations, we evaluate specific market characteristics, demographics, traffic patterns, co-tenants and growth potential. Our development approach has proven that First Watch has tremendous portability across markets, with new restaurants boasting a consistent and strong average unit volume across all geographies. First Watch's top 10% of restaurants in terms of sales, span 13 states and 24 designated market areas. The average annual sales volumes of our new restaurants outpace the system average, and we expect to sustain the performance through quality real estate selection and the introduction of features and operational practices designed to efficiently serve more demand.

Our long-term growth strategy includes the acquisition of First Watch restaurants operated by certain of our franchisees. To that end, during 2025, we acquired 19 operating restaurants along with development and territory rights in two separate transactions. We believe the Company's operation of the restaurants acquired from our franchisees as well as development in the reacquired territory, provides substantial opportunity to realize new Company value. At December 28, 2025, we had 9 franchisees operating 73 restaurants with 17 total new restaurant development obligations. At December 28, 2025, 12 franchise-owned restaurants are subject to our option to purchase.

Our return on invested capital reflects our disciplined focus on building sales and traffic through the core elements of the First Watch experience - serving high-quality food, delivering memorable service, and providing an inviting atmosphere.

We are vulnerable to changes in economic conditions and consumer preferences that could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our failure to manage our growth effectively could harm our business and results of operations.
Opening new restaurants in existing markets may adversely impact sales at our and our franchisees' existing restaurants.
A decline in visitors to any of the retail centers, lifestyle centers, or entertainment centers where our restaurants are located could adversely affect our restaurant sales.
Our same-restaurant sales growth and same-restaurant traffic growth may be lower than we expect in future periods.
Changes in the cost of food could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
New restaurants may not be profitable or may close, and the performance of our restaurants that we have experienced in the past may not be indicative of future results.
Food safety and food-borne illness concerns may have an adverse effect on our business by decreasing sales and increasing costs.
The financial performance of our franchisees can have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We have limited control with respect to the operations of our franchisees, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
If we are unable to maintain good relationships with our franchisees due to conflicts of interest or otherwise, revenues could decrease and we may be unable to expand our presence in certain markets.
Our system-wide restaurant base is geographically concentrated in the southeast portion of the United States, and we could be adversely affected by conditions specific to that region.
Damage to our reputation and negative publicity could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Information technology system failures or breaches of our network security could interrupt our operations and have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We face potential liability with our gift cards under the property laws of some states.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks described below in addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the sections titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," "Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk" and our consolidated financial statements and related notes. If any of the risks and uncertainties described in the cautionary factors below actually occur or continue to occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flow and the trading price of our common stock could be materially and adversely affected. The considerations and risks that follow are organized within relevant headings but may be relevant to other headings as well. Moreover, the risks below are not the only risks we face and additional risks not currently known to us or that we presently deem immaterial may emerge or become material at any time and may adversely impact our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations or cash flow or the trading price of our common stock.
Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, including those outside of our control, that could cause our actual results to be harmed. These risks include the following:
•our vulnerability to changes in economic conditions, consumer preferences and other factors, many of which are largely outside of our control
•our inability to open new restaurants in new and existing markets or to operate them as profitably as we have experienced in the past
•our inability to effectively manage our growth
•opening new restaurants in existing markets may adversely impact sales at our and our franchisees' existing restaurants

paragraphs: First Watch is an award-winning Daytime Dining concept serving made-to-order breakfast, brunch and lunch using fresh ingredients. Our common stock trades on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "FWRG." A recipient of many local "Best Breakfast" and "Best Brunch" accolades, First Watch's award-winning chef-driven menu includes elevated executions of classic favorites for breakfast, brunch and lunch. For four consecutive years, First Watch has been named a Top 100 Most Loved Workplace® by the Best Practice Institute, and in 2025, was named the #1 Most Loved Workplace for the second year in a row, featured in The Wall Street Journal. Also, in 2025, First Watch was named one of Yelp's Most-Loved Brands nationwide.

We operate and franchise restaurants in 32 states under the "First Watch" trade name and as of December 28, 2025, had 560 company-owned restaurants and 73 franchise-owned restaurants. We do not operate outside of the United States.

Our 52- or 53-week fiscal years end on the last Sunday of each calendar year. Our fiscal quarters are comprised of 13 weeks each and end on the 13th Sunday of each quarter, except for 53-week years, during which the fourth quarter ends on the 14th Sunday of the fourth quarter. All references to 2025 and 2024 reflect the results of the 52-week fiscal years ended December 28, 2025 and December 29, 2024, respectively. All references to 2023 reflect the results of the 53-week fiscal year ended December 31, 2023 unless otherwise stated. We report financial and operating information in one segment.

This section of this Annual Report on the Form 10-K generally discusses Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024 and year-over-year comparisons between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024. A discussion of Fiscal 2023 and year-over-year comparisons between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023 that are not included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K can be found in Part II, Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as filed with the SEC on March 5, 2024.

Throughout this"Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" we commonly discuss the following key operating metrics that we believe will drive our financial results and long-term growth model. We believe these metrics are useful to investors because our Management uses these metrics to evaluate performance and assess the growth of our business as well as the effectiveness of our marketing and operational strategies.

New Restaurant Openings ("NROs"): the number of new company-owned First Watch restaurants commencing operations during the period. Management reviews the number of new restaurants to assess new restaurant growth and company-owned restaurant sales.

Same-Restaurant Sales Growth: the percentage change in year-over-year restaurant sales (excluding gift card breakage) for the comparable restaurant base, which we define as the number of company-owned First Watch branded restaurants open for 18 months or longer as of the beginning of the fiscal year ("Comparable Restaurant Base"). This operating metric compares the 52-week periods ended December 28, 2025, December 29, 2024 and December 31, 2023, rather than, the 53-week fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, in order to compare like-for-like periods. For the 52-weeks ended December 28, 2025, December 29, 2024 and December 31, 2023 there were 381, 344 and 327 restaurants, in our Comparable Restaurant Base, respectively. Measuring our same-restaurant sales growth allows Management to evaluate the performance of our existing restaurant base. We believe this measure is useful for investors to provide a consistent comparison of restaurant sales results and trends across periods within our core, established restaurant base, unaffected by results of store openings, closings and other transitional changes.

Same-Restaurant Traffic Growth: the percentage change in year-over-year traffic counts using the Comparable Restaurant Base. This operating metric compares the 52-week periods ended December 28, 2025, December 29, 2024 and December 31, 2023, - (rather than the 53-week fiscal year ended December 31, 2023), in order to compare like-for-like periods. Measuring our same-restaurant traffic growth allows our Management to evaluate the performance of our existing

restaurant base. We believe this measure is useful for investors because same-restaurant traffic provides an indicator as to the development of our brand and the effectiveness of our marketing strategy.

Average Unit Volume ("AUV"): the total restaurant sales (excluding gift card breakage) recognized in the Comparable Restaurant Base, divided by the number of restaurants in the Comparable Restaurant Base during the period. This measurement allows Management to assess changes in consumer spending patterns at our restaurants and the overall performance of our restaurant base.

To supplement the consolidated financial statements, which are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP"), we use the following non-GAAP measures, which present operating results on an adjusted basis: (i) Adjusted EBITDA, (ii) Adjusted EBITDA margin, (iii) Restaurant level operating profit and (iv) Restaurant level operating profit margin. Our presentation of these non-GAAP measures includes isolating the effects of some items that are either nonrecurring in nature or have no meaningful correlation to our ongoing core operating performance. These supplemental measures of performance are not required by or presented in accordance with GAAP. Management believes these non-GAAP measures provide investors with additional visibility into our operations, facilitate analysis and comparisons of our ongoing business operations because they exclude items that may not be indicative of our ongoing operating performance, help to identify operational trends and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by Management in our financial and operational decision making. Our non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies and have important limitations as analytical tools. These non-GAAP measures should not be considered in isolation or as substitutes for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP as they may not provide a complete understanding of our performance. These non-GAAP measures should be reviewed in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP.

We use Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin (i) as factors in evaluating management's performance when determining incentive compensation, (ii) to evaluate our operating results and the effectiveness of our business strategies and (iii) internally as benchmarks to compare our performance to that of our competitors.

We use Restaurant level operating profit and Restaurant level operating profit margin (i) to evaluate the performance and profitability of operating restaurants, individually and in the aggregate, and (ii) to make decisions regarding future spending and other operational decisions.

Adjusted EBITDA: represents Net income before depreciation and amortization, interest expense, income taxes and items that we do not consider in our evaluation of ongoing core operating performance as identified in the reconciliation of Net income, the most directly comparable measure in accordance with GAAP, to Adjusted EBITDA, included in the section Non-GAAP Financial Measure Reconciliations below.

{'translated_text': '經驗豐富、熱忱的領導團隊及深厚的人才儲備'}
paragraphs: First Watch Restaurant Group, Inc. 為一家設立於特拉華州的控股公司。除非文意另有明確要求，否則 "we," "us," "our," "First Watch," the "Company," "Management" 以及其他類似用語均指 First Watch Restaurant Group, Inc.，除非另有說明，否則亦包括其所有子公司。

自1983年開店以來，我們一直是日間用餐的先驅者，提供現點現做、以最新鮮食材製作的早餐、早午餐與午餐。我們的品牌建立在對運營卓越的承諾、以新鮮且持續進化的菜單為核心的料理使命，以及我們的 "You First" 文化之上。我們專注於日間單一班次，使我們能夠優化餐廳運作，並在2025年每間餐廳於每天僅7.5小時內產生平均2.3 百萬美元的銷售額。這種日間專注也為我們帶來競爭優勢，使我們能夠吸引並留住對餐飲業熱情且傾向於我們 "No Night Shifts Ever" 方針的員工，以及其他有吸引力的福利。
截至2025年12月28日，我們共有633間餐廳，分佈於32個州，其中560間為本公司所有，73間為特許經營權所有。

每天清晨，數千名員工在天未亮時便抵達餐廳，切削並榨取新鮮水果與蔬菜，烘烤馬芬，製作我們的新鮮咖啡，並從頭開始調製法式吐司的麵糊。每一道餐點皆為現點現做，並以細心的態度準備。我們的廚房不使用微波爐、熱燈或油炸機。在First Watch，我們以追求新鮮為動力，這體現在我們的料理與採購哲學 "Follow the Sun" 中。根據此哲學，我們的菜單靈感來自四季，每年會更換四到五次。我們的季節性菜單常被顧客視為First Watch體驗的核心元素，其中包括如帕瑪森起司與帕爾馬火腿吐司、奇米丘裏牛排蛋鬆餅，以及布魯克林早餐三明治等經典項目。
這些季節性餐點與我們的獲獎 chef 驅動型菜單並列，該菜單包含對早餐、早午餐與午餐經典項目升級的版本，例如我們的高蛋白早餐藜麥碗、奇基香腸與牛油果吐司。我們的菜單也包含新鮮果汁，這些果汁我們每天早晨現榨，包括 Morning Meditation 和 Kale Tonic。

在超過四十年的時間裡，我們已經培養出一種以 "You First" 為基礎的組織文化，將服務他人放在首位。作為一家公司，我們將員工視為第一優先，並賦予他們做任何事情的權力，以確保顧客獲得最佳服務。根據我們的願景 "Create Amazing Opportunities for Our People"，我們也努力為員工提供晉升機會與有意義的關係，並重視個人與專業成長，使員工得以茁壯成長。我們相信，我們的作法與運營模式使我們能夠留住並吸引業界最優秀的員工，並成為我們全國性需求增長的關鍵因素。因此，我們為過去幾十年所獲得的許多以人為本的獎項與榮譽感到自豪。在連續四年，First Watch 被評選為 Best Practice Institute 所公佈的 Top 100 Most Loved Workplace®，而在2025年，我們再次被評選為年度第一名 Most Loved Workplace，並在《華爾街日報》上報導。此外，在2025年，First Watch 被評選為 Yelp 全國最受喜愛的品牌之一。
我們也透過將 "You First" 文化延伸至重要的組織與事務，來回饋我們員工與社區所關心的事物。除了在服務社區的各個地方進行多樣的慈善活動，First Watch 也透過關鍵的計畫來創造正面影響，這影響不僅在外部，也在我們組織內：
•Project Sunrise：透過此計畫，我們從哥倫比亞的女性所有咖啡莊園採購咖啡豆，並每年支付品質激勵獎金給農民，以進一步支持他們的高品質生產。此計畫使這些女性領導者得以將資金重新投資於他們的社區。
•兒童癌症研究：我們將每銷售一份 First Watch 兒童餐所得的一部分捐贈給 V 基金會，以支持並推動兒童癌症研究。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們已捐贈約 2.0 百萬美元用以支持此重要計畫。
•You First 基金：於 2020 年設立，You First 基金提供符合資格的員工因符合資格的災難所遭遇個人困難之獎學金。此基金旨在支持員工及其直屬家屬在最迫切需要之時，並透過每銷售一份兒童餐所得的一部分，以及本公司、員工及其他人士之捐款來資助。自設立以來，此基金已為員工提供超過 1.1 百萬美元之困難獎學金。

我們認為 First Watch 在美國本土擁有超過 2,200 家餐廳之潛力。2021 年，First Watch 被 FSR 雜誌評選為美國成長最快的全服務餐廳公司，根據單位成長數量。2025 年，我們持續實現此潛力，透過開設 64 家本公司所有及特許經營之餐廳，我們 collectively 稱為 "system-wide" 餐廳，橫跨 23 個州。我們的成長策略預期將增加每年新開 system-wide 餐廳之數量。

在選擇新據點時，我們評估特定市場特徵、人口統計、交通模式、共租戶及成長潛力。我們的發展方式已證明 First Watch 在各市場具有極大之可移植性，新餐廳在所有地理區域均表現出一致且強勁之平均單位銷售額。First Watch 銷售表現前 10% 之餐廳，橫跨 13 個州及 24 個指定市場區域。我們新餐廳之平均年銷售額高於系統平均，我們預期透過優質不動產選擇及引入特色與作業方式，以提高效率來維持此表現。

我們的長期成長策略包括收購由部分特許經營者經營之 First Watch 餐廳。為此，於 2025 年，我們透過兩筆獨立交易收購 19 家營運中之餐廳，以及開發與地區權。我們認為本公司經營從特許經營者收購之餐廳，以及在重新取得地區之開發，提供實現新公司價值之重大機會。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們有 9 家特許經營者經營 73 家餐廳，並有 17 家總計新餐廳開發義務。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，有 12 家特許經營之餐廳屬於本公司購入選擇權範疇。
我們之投資資本回報率反映我們專注於透過 First Watch 經驗之核心要素來提升銷售與人流量之謹慎策略 - 提供高品質食物、提供難忘服務，以及提供吸引人的氛圍。

headings: 特許經營新餐廳開幕數（"特許經營新餐廳開幕數"）：於該期間內開始營運的新特許經營First Watch餐廳數量。
系統內餐廳數：包含所有本公司所有及特許經營餐廳的總數。
系統內銷售額：包含本公司所有及特許經營餐廳的餐廳銷售額。我們不將特許經營餐廳的餐廳銷售額認列為收入。
2025年商品通貨膨脹率為5.0%，主要由蛋、咖啡、牛油果及香腸等商品驅動。我們預期2026年商品價格將較前一年增加約1%至3%，主要與咖啡相關。

paragraphs: First Watch 是一家獲獎肯定的午間用餐概念，提供客製化早餐、早午餐與午餐，使用新鮮食材。我們的普通股在 Nasdaq 上交易，股票代碼為 "FWRG." First Watch 獲得多項當地 "最佳早餐" 與 "最佳早午餐" 種種榮譽，其獲獎肯定的主廚驅動式菜單包含升級版的經典餐點，用於早餐、早午餐與午餐。連續四年，First Watch 被評為 Best Practice Institute 所公佈的 Top 100 Most Loved Workplace®，並於 2025 年再次獲選為年度第一名最受喜愛的工作場所，並在 The Wall Street Journal 上報導。此外，於 2025 年，First Watch 被評為 Yelp 全美最受喜愛的品牌之一。
我們在 32 個州運營與特許經營的餐廳，品牌為 "First Watch"，截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，我們擁有 560 家自有餐廳與 73 家特許經營餐廳。我們不運營美國以外的地區。

我們的財務年度為 52 或 53 週，於每個曆年最後一個星期日結束。我們的財務季度由 13 週組成，於每個季度的第 13 個星期日結束，除非是 53 週的年份，則第四季於該季度的第 14 個星期日結束。所有提及 2025 與 2024 的內容，均反映 2025 年 12 月 28 日結束的 52 週財務年度與 2024 年 12 月 29 日結束的 52 週財務年度的結果。所有提及 2023 的內容，均反映 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的 53 週財務年度的結果，除非另有說明。我們以一個應報告分部報告財務與營運資訊。

本年度報告 10-K 的此部分一般討論財務年度 2025 與財務年度 2024，以及財務年度 2025 與財務年度 2024 的年對年比較。財務年度 2023 與財務年度 2024 與財務年度 2023 的年對年比較，未包含於本年度報告 10-K 中，可於 Part II, Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" 中找到，該部分為我們 2023 年財務年度的年度報告 10-K，於 2024 年 3 月 5 日提交至 SEC。
在本 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" 中，我們常討論以下關鍵營運指標，我們認為這些指標將驅動我們的財務結果與長期成長模式。我們認為這些指標對投資者而言是有用的，因為我們的管理階層使用這些指標來評估表現與評估我們業務的成長，以及我們行銷與營運策略的成效。
新餐廳開幕 ("NROs"): 期間內新開幕的自有 First Watch 餐廳數量。管理階層會檢視新餐廳數量，以評估新餐廳成長與自有餐廳銷售額。

相同餐廳銷售成長: 比較年度餐廳銷售額 (扣除禮券折損) 的年對年變動百分比，我們定義為在財務年度開始時已營運 18 個月或以上的自有 First Watch 品牌餐廳數量 ("Comparable Restaurant Base"). 這個營運指標比較 2025 年 12 月 28 日結束的 52 週期間、2024 年 12 月 29 日結束的 52 週期間與 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的 53 週期間，而非 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的 53 週財務年度，以比較相同期間。於 2025 年 12 月 28 日結束的 52 週期間、2024 年 12 月 29 日結束的 52 週期間與 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的 53 週期間，我們的 Comparable Restaurant Base 分別有 381 家、344 家與 327 家餐廳。測量我們的相同餐廳銷售成長，使管理階層能評估我們現有餐廳基礎的表現。我們認為此指標對投資者而言是有用的，以提供一致的餐廳銷售結果與趨勢比較，不受新店開幕、關閉及其他過渡性變動的影響。

相同餐廳人流量成長: 比較年度人流量的年對年變動百分比，使用 Comparable Restaurant Base。這個營運指標比較 2025 年 12 月 28 日結束的 52 週期間、2024 年 12 月 29 日結束的 52 週期間與 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的 53 週期間，而非 2023 年 12 月 31 日結束的 53 週財務年度，以比較相同期間。測量我們的相同餐廳人流量成長，使我們的管理階層能評估我們現有
餐廳基準。我們認為這個指標對投資人而言是有用的，因為同店客流量可以作為我們品牌發展及行銷策略成效的指標。
平均單店營收（"AUV"）：指在可比餐廳基準中認列的總餐廳銷售額（扣除禮券折損），除以可比餐廳基準中該期間的餐廳數量。這個指標讓管理階層能夠評估消費者在餐廳的支出模式變化以及我們餐廳基準的整體表現。

為補充根據美國通用會計原則（"GAAP"）編製的合併財務報表，我們使用以下非GAAP指標，這些指標以調整後的基礎呈現營運結果：(i) 調整後營運資金（Adjusted EBITDA），(ii) 調整後營運資金率（Adjusted EBITDA margin），(iii) 餐廳層級營運利潤，以及 (iv) 餐廳層級營運利潤率。我們呈現這些非GAAP指標時，會將一些項目影響隔離出來，這些項目或是非經常性，或是與我們持續核心營運表現無明顯關聯。這些補充性的績效指標並非根據GAAP規定或呈現。管理階層認為這些非GAAP指標可為投資人提供額外的運營透明度，有助於分析與比較我們持續的業務運作，因為它們排除了可能無法反映我們持續營運表現的項目，有助於識別運營趨勢，並提高管理階層在財務與運營決策中使用關鍵指標的透明度。我們的非GAAP指標可能與其他公司使用之類似名稱的指標不具可比性，且作為分析工具時有其重要限制。這些非GAAP指標不應孤立地考慮，也不應作為分析我們根據GAAP報告結果的替代方案，因為它們可能無法完全反映我們的表現。這些非GAAP指標應與根據GAAP編製的合併財務報表一併審閱。
我們使用調整後營運資金（Adjusted EBITDA）與調整後營運資金率（Adjusted EBITDA margin）(i) 作為評估管理階層表現並決定激勵報酬的考量因素，(ii) 用以評估我們的營運結果與業務策略的成效，以及 (iii) 內部作為與競爭對手錶現比較的參考基準。
我們使用餐廳層級營運利潤與餐廳層級營運利潤率 (i) 用以評估個別及整體餐廳的營運表現與獲利能力，以及 (ii) 用以決定未來支出及其他運營決策。
調整後營運資金（Adjusted EBITDA）：指淨收入扣除折舊與攤銷、利息支出、所得稅及我們在評估持續核心營運表現時不考慮的項目，如根據GAAP最直接可比的指標淨收入，與調整後營運資金的對應關係，包含於下述「非GAAP財務指標明細」部分。

我們易受總體經濟條件及消費者偏好的變動影響，這可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
若我們無法有效管理成長，可能會損害我們的業務及營運成果。
在現有市場開設新餐廳可能會對我們及我們特許經營者的現有餐廳銷售造成負面影響。
若任何零售中心、生活風格中心或娛樂中心的訪客數量下降，可能會對我們的餐廳銷售造成不利影響。
我們的同店銷售成長及同店人流量成長可能低於我們未來期間的預期。
食品成本的變動可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
新開設的餐廳可能無法獲利或關閉，且我們過去所經驗的餐廳營運表現可能無法反映未來結果。
食品安全及食源性疾病相關問題可能對我們的業務產生負面影響，導致銷售額下降且成本增加。
我們特許經營者的財務表現可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大負面影響。
我們對特許經營者的營運控制有限，這可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大負面影響。
若因利益衝突或其他原因無法維持與特許經營者良好的關係，收入可能減少，且我們可能無法在某些市場擴大經營據點。
我們的系統性餐廳據點地理上集中於美國南部東部地區，我們可能因該地區特定情況而受到負面影響。
我們聲譽受損及負面宣傳可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大負面影響。
資訊科技系統故障或網路安全遭入侵可能中斷我們的營運，並對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大負面影響。

paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，並配合本年度10-K表報表中其他資訊，包括標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」、「市場風險之量化與質化揭露」以及我們合併財務報表與相關附註之內容。若下列所描述的風險與不確定性有任何實際發生或持續發生，將可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流，以及普通股之交易價格造成重大且不利之影響。以下所列之考量與風險，已依照相關標題歸類，但可能同時與其他標題相關。此外，下列風險並非本公司所面臨之唯一風險，且可能有其他尚未為本公司所知悉或目前認為不重要之風險，未來可能出現或變得重要，並可能對本公司之業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流，或普通股之交易價格造成不利影響。
本公司業務面臨許多風險與不確定性，包括一些超出本公司控制範圍之因素，這些風險可能對本公司實際之營運成果造成損害。這些風險包括以下內容：
•本公司對經濟條件變動、消費者偏好及其他因素之脆弱性，其中許多因素 largely outside of our control
•本公司無法在新市場或現有市場開設新餐廳，或無法以過去所經驗之獲利程度來營運這些餐廳
•本公司無法有效管理本公司之成長
•在現有市場開設新餐廳可能對本公司及特許經營商之現有餐廳銷售造成負面影響
